{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, following the no-database line of thinking. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

HIS WORDS: *"if we remove a db and go strictly with in-memory, then exporting the graph becomes a necessary step. curious if we at every instance the reflow2 graph is changed, that the graph is automatically exported to the git repo (don't have to do a git commit/push with every export)."*

⭐ THE DISTINCTION HE DREW IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, and it is easy to miss: **write to the WORKING TREE, not to git history.** Those are different acts. The file landing in the repo gives durability — it survives the process dying, it is on a disk somebody backs up, and it is where every existing reader (`reflow2_check.py`, `compare_designs`, the merge driver) already looks. Committing it is a separate, human, deliberate act. Nothing about continuous export requires continuous history.

⭐⭐ THE OBJECTION THAT KILLED THIS ROAD IS MEASURED AWAY, TODAY. `dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy` listed "export on every write" FIRST and recorded it as **dead**, on the hosted-tier node's ground that a whole-document write is "correct for an archival action and fatal on a per-change path". That was true when a full export cost seconds. Measured 2026-08-25 after two fixes (#330 and #331):

    build export doc   1,137 ms  ->  236 ms
    serialize to JSON     31 ms  ->   29 ms
    TOTAL full export  1,168 ms  ->  265 ms

**A whole-document export of the largest design in existence is a quarter of a second.** A typical design would be a small fraction of that. The road was closed on a number that is no longer the number.

🛑 BUT IT COLLIDES HEAD-ON WITH AN ACCEPTED DECISION. `dec:export-once-per-pr` is ACCEPTED: *"A branch may hold as many commits as it likes; exactly ONE of them may write docs/design/reflow2.json, and it should be the last."* Its reason is the lineage chain — `prev_content_hash` links each export to the one it replaced, and squash-merge collapses the branch to one commit, so intermediate links point at content no commit contains and the chain becomes unfollowable. **Auto-exporting on every graph change writes that file hundreds of times per session**, so the discipline stops being enforceable by construction rather than by forgetting.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ THE ROAD RECOMMENDED, 2026-08-25 — **TWO FILES**, and it is an AGENT'S
FINDING, NOT A DECISION. Anthony asked for the recommendation on the record;
recording it does not settle it, and the node stays `proposed`.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

**Separate the thing that keeps you safe from the thing that goes in git.**

- A **LIVE FILE** — written continuously (or debounced), **gitignored**, in `.reflow2/`. Pure durability. Nothing chains it, nobody diffs it, it never appears in `git status`. It needs no new format: it is the same export document.
- The **COMMITTED EXPORT** — `docs/design/reflow2.json`, written once, deliberately, exactly as today. The RECORD: the lineage chain, what a PR carries, what a reviewer reads.

IT ANSWERS ALL FOUR OBJECTIONS AT ONCE, which is why it is preferred over debounce-alone or chain-at-commit:
1. The lineage chain stays meaningful, because only deliberate exports chain. `dec:export-once-per-pr` survives UNCHANGED rather than being amended — the collision disappears instead of being negotiated.
2. The working tree stays clean, so half-finished design state cannot be committed by accident.
3. `req:stale-seat-knows` keeps guarding an occasional deliberate act instead of running on a hot path.
4. `git diff docs/design/reflow2.json` keeps meaning *"what this session decided to record"* rather than everything that happened including what was retracted.

⭐⭐ AND THE DURABILITY ARGUMENT INVERTS ON INSPECTION — the strongest reason for the road, found while writing this up. **Today's setup already has the gap this is accused of introducing.** reflow2 keeps two copies: the RocksDB store and the export. The store protects against the PROCESS dying; it does NOT protect against the directory dying, and `loop_status` says so on every call — *"The file is the only copy that survives losing the graph directory."* So the copy that survives real loss is the export, **and today it is written only when somebody remembers**. Measured on this very session: nine nodes sat unexported for hours.

    protects against:        process crash   disk/machine loss   written
    today   RocksDB store         yes              NO            continuously
    today   export file           yes              yes           WHEN SOMEBODY REMEMBERS
    two-file  live file           yes              yes           continuously
    two-file  committed export    yes              yes           deliberately

⇒ Anthony's reading is right, and stronger than he put it: this is not a trade of durability for convenience. **The two-file shape CLOSES a durability gap that exists today.** What is given up is only the window between one live-file write and the next — one change, or a few seconds under a debounce, which is the resilience an editor or a browser tab gives and nobody calls those unreliable. His own framing: *"most things are not that resilient to crashes, so I would expect that reflow2 keeps the same level of resilience as most other services."*

⚠️ WHAT THE RECOMMENDATION DOES NOT COVER, stated so it is not read as settled:
- **265 ms is THIS design's number, the largest in existence.** Per-change export at that size adds a quarter-second to every write. Debounce — write on idle, or at most every N seconds — rather than literally per change, and MEASURE a typical-sized design before assuming the figure generalises. (Two performance predictions were wrong today before being measured; the habit is the finding.)
- **Where the live file lives when there is no repo.** A hosted tenant at flo2 has no working tree; the same shape needs an object-store answer, which `dec:idea-a-hosted-tier-of-many-single-writer-tenants` holds.
- **`last_synced` still has to endure.** `fact:a-hydrated-seat-keeps-every-confirmation-date-and-loses-only-its-sync-state` measured that a hydrated seat loses exactly this one map; a live file carries the design, not the sidecar, so that remains a separate loose end.

ROADS NOT TAKEN, kept with their reasoning:
- **Export on every write, one file.** Simplest, and it is what breaks `dec:export-once-per-pr` outright plus all four objections above.
- **Advance the lineage chain on COMMIT rather than on write.** Coherent — the chain's purpose is to relate committed records — but it puts the chain's correctness in git's hands rather than reflow2's, and reflow2 cannot see a commit.
- **Recompute the chain at commit time** from whatever file is there. Same objection, plus it needs a hook nobody has.
- **Do nothing; keep the store authoritative.** Costs nothing and keeps the manual-export durability gap the table above measures.

RECORDED AS A QUESTION WITH A RECOMMENDED ROAD, NOT AS A CONCLUSION.","name":"OPEN — with no database, should every graph change auto-export to the working tree (no commit, no push)?
